claim: Hidden states of code models linearly encode the execution correctness of generated code above chance (reported AUCs or accuracies well above random across autoregressive, diffusion, agentic, and pre-generation settings).
scope: Code with execution labels; 8+ independent groups after collapsing Devanbu/Nadi and Bui/Vu clusters

claim: Stated (verbal or reflective) confidence of code models is poorly calibrated, overconfident, or inconsistent as a predictor of execution correctness, especially for small open instruct models.
scope: Code with execution labels; Ribeiro et al. (same Devanbu/Nadi cluster as 240202047) counted once

claim: Token-level likelihood or entropy is a weak discriminator of pass versus fail across problems on code (AUROC near or below about 0.70 in most reported settings).
scope: Code with execution labels; exceptions are within-task mutant ranking and token-localization uses

claim: NLI- or embedding-based semantic entropy transferred from NLG fails on code; clustering sampled programs by execution behavior or symbolic equivalence is needed for sampled agreement to track correctness.
scope: Code with execution labels; assessing-correctness and using-semantic-distance may share the Sharma and David group, so only one is listed

claim: Binned ECE alone is a misleading calibration measure: it can be near zero for base-rate or collapsed predictors and decouples from discrimination, so resolution, Brier skill, or AUROC must be reported alongside it.
scope: Mixed: code with execution labels (240202047, verbalized-uncertainty, characterizing-overconfident) and general-domain

claim: Calibration and discrimination dissociate: post-hoc recalibration improves calibration error or Brier but does not improve ranking by correctness, and cannot recover information the score has lost.
scope: Mixed: code (generation and classification) plus general statistical theory

claim: Benchmark test suites are thin enough that execution labels carry false passes; strengthening tests lowers measured pass rates and can change model rankings.
scope: Code with execution labels (function-level, repository-level, text-to-SQL)

claim: LLM-written tests are not independent verifiers: they inherit the generator's blind spots, often fail to execute or carry wrong oracles, and agreement-based selection fails when samples share correlated errors.
scope: Code with execution labels; duplicate notes for verification-trap and beyond-coverage counted once

claim: Pooled AUROC of code and agent correctness predictors is dominated by problem difficulty; within-problem or within-run discrimination is much weaker.
scope: Code with execution labels; disentangling, hard-issue, and continue-or-restart may share authors (not confirmed in the redundancy audit), so independence rests on which-signals and the diffusion probe paper plus at least one agent paper

claim: Outside code, hidden-state probes or internal estimators predict answer correctness better than verbalized confidence.
scope: General-domain (math, factual QA, forecasting, true/false statements); no execution labels

claim: Post-training (instruction tuning, RLHF, RL with verifiable rewards) degrades token-probability calibration relative to the base model in general NLP.
scope: General-domain (MMLU, QA, math); code evidence limited to characterizing-overconfident at token level

claim: Verbal confidence from small or mid-size instruct models is often degenerate (saturated near a ceiling or collapsed into few values), and its behavior depends on elicitation format.
scope: Mixed: code (verbalized-uncertainty) and general-domain; verbal-confidence-saturation and measurement-validity may share an author line (pre-registered validity series), counted cautiously

claim: Under a matched sampling budget, self-repair with feedback is often no better than independent resampling on code.
Agreement- or confidence-based adaptive sampling and early stopping reduce compute at near-equal accuracy on mostly solvable reasoning workloads.
scope: Mostly general-domain math and reasoning (lets-sample includes code datasets); contested for hard workloads by give-up-to-get-more

claim: Execution-based selection among sampled programs (generated-test agreement, behavior clustering, execution-result MBR, execution-aware verifiers) improves over plain generation.
Fine-grained (token- or line-level) localization of likely-faulty code from model signals is feasible and already demonstrated.
scope: Code; labels are repair patches, edits, or execution outcomes rather than per-requirement test groups

claim: Signal-detection and psychometric framings (type-2 AUROC, meta-d', sensitivity versus bias, validity screening) are already applied to LLM confidence outside code.
scope: General-domain; none on code with execution labels
